messages:
Jane (support): heads-up — multiple customers reporting 504s and elevated retries to the hosted inference API in us-east-1 and us-west-2 since ~05:10 UTC. customer impact: increased client-side retries, some auth failures after retries. stacktrace from a customer attached (see logs). any initial thoughts? :exclamation:

Maya (eng): seeing a correlated bump in proxy 504 latencies in hosted-gateway-usw2. metrics: 99th p50 -> p99 spiked from 120ms to ~2.3s, request timeouts up. throwing this into the incident channel. tagging @Tomas for SRE/infra triage.

Tomas (SRE): grabbing gateway logs now. early hypothesis: transient TCP stalls / reordering on peered paths causing backend TCP timeouts -> haproxy/GW returns 504. Also seeing a lot of connection resets at the gateway level. Will run active repro from our vantage.

Olivia (infra): I can repro a couple 504s from within our VPC when hitting the same route. curl shows incomplete TLS handshakes occasionally. Here's a quick reproduce command we're using: 

```
curl -vvv -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDBWOOD_TEST_TOKEN" https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -d '{"input":"test"}' --max-time 10
```

Output includes repeated TLS renegotiation and then HTTP/2 stream reset.

Ryan (network): I pulled traceroutes from a few affected hosts. noticed high jitter and packet reordering on one of the transit peers between our edge and VeloNet (peer-id: 20345). sample traceroute below (times in ms):

```
traceroute to api-gw.ve3.velonet (203.45.67.89), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.3.0.1 (10.3.0.1)  0.411 ms 0.352 ms 0.301 ms
 2  198.51.100.2 (198.51.100.2)  1.12 ms 1.09 ms 1.05 ms
 3  203.45.67.1 (203.45.67.1)  2.34 ms 20.12 ms 0.83 ms  <-- large variance
 4  203.45.67.89 (203.45.67.89)  2.40 ms 0.98 ms 35.65 ms
```

Pattern: microbursts/jitter around hop 3. Also saw occasional TTL changes suggesting ECMP path shifts.

eng-sre-bot: automated alert: spike in 504s detected for route /v1/generate in us-west-2. Event id: evt-1892. Please follow incident runbook.

Maya (eng): can we confirm whether this is local gateway CPU saturation or network? CPU on gateway nodes is normal, only 40-55% during peaks. kernel retransmits are spiking.

Tomas (SRE): kernel tcp_retrans_out and tcp_retrans_fail counters are elevated on edge proxies. suggests packet loss rather than app-level bug. Also seeing more TLS session renegotiations > likely due to lost packets during handshake.

Jane (support): customers are reporting different symptoms — some see 502s then 504s after retries, others get client-side auth errors after repeated attempts. are we losing sessions that invalidate short-lived tokens?

Olivia (infra): short-lived tokens shouldn't expire mid-handshake, but if retry logic triggers new connections during partial handshakes it can look like auth failures.

Ryan (network): opened ticket with VeloNet peering ops (ticket: VN-7821). initial response: "investigating microbursts on peering circuit, possible buffer misconfiguration on PE". They asked for pcap/snmp sflow from our peering router — attaching flow samples via secure share.

Maya (eng): mitigation plan proposals: 1) temporarily shift customer traffic to alternate peer via BGP preference (slow failover) 2) enable connection draining and increase backend timeouts to reduce client retries 3) roll gateway proxies to nodes in alternate AZs that egress via different peering. thoughts?

Tomas (SRE): doing 2) now — increasing haproxy timeout http-request and http-server by +2s to reduce 504s from transient stalls. Not ideal long term but lowers customer-visible errors. Pushing config in canary to 2 proxies.

Olivia (infra): I can initiate 3) — draining and moving a small subset of instances to use a different egress route. will monitor error rate.

eng-sre-bot: deploy triggered: haproxy-timeout-bump -> canary on hosted-gw-usw2-azb.

VeloNet-peering-bot: update from VeloNet: "we're seeing intermittent packet reordering tied to recent config push on PE routers; engineers rolling back change in progress (ETA 12-18 minutes)."

Jane (support): relaying rollback ETA to Tier 2 customers, asking for logs and example request ids. pls include request ids so we can correlate.

Maya (eng): quick log extract from gateway showing TLS resets and backend connection aborts: 

```
[2026-03-15T05:18:02Z] gw-proxy-3 haproxy: frontend HTTP-in conns=1 addr=10.1.5.8:53222 -> backend=hosted-backend/10.2.3.7 status=504 code=H/SC
[2026-03-15T05:18:03Z] gw-proxy-3 kernel: TCP: possible reordering src=203.45.67.89 dst=10.2.3.7 seq=...
[2026-03-15T05:18:05Z] gw-proxy-3 ssl: TLS alert: handshake failure (unexpected record)
```

Tomas (SRE): after the timeout bump and the canary shift, error rate on the canary dropped by ~60% within 4m. rolling the timeout bump cluster-wide now while we wait for VeloNet rollback confirmation.

Ryan (network): VeloNet confirms rollback complete at 05:32 UTC. they report "metrics returned to baseline, packet reordering reduced". recommending we keep traffic on alternate peer for 10m to validate.

Olivia (infra): traffic metrics look stable. 5xx counts trending back to normal. keeping an eye on TLS handshake failure counters.

Jane (support): passing update to customers: mitigation applied (timeouts increased + partial egress shift). VeloNet applied rollback; monitoring for full recovery. Customers asked for RCA and timeline — we should start drafting.

Maya (eng): immediate next steps: - keep timeouts longer for 1 hour then revert if stable - validate token lifetime behavior in retry cases - coordinate with VeloNet for postmortem and ask for their config change diff - draft customer-facing summary (support + PR)

Tomas (SRE): owners: Maya (eng) will draft tech RCA, Jane (support) will draft customer summary, Ryan (network) to follow up with VeloNet for config details. tagging followups in the incident tracker.

eng-sre-bot: incident EVT-1892 status -> mitigated. will transition to post-incident review channel.

Jane (support): thanks all. please paste any request ids or extra logs here for the RCA. closing thread in 30m if no regressions. :thumbsup:
